what: Draws the element’s text (wordmark) in that element’s typeface, slices it into seven horizontal bands, turns each continuous ink span in a band into a round-ended pill bar, and redraws it as SVG, so the letters look like stacked horizontal bars. Every 1s each bar slides to its own random position within ±.4rem (±.7rem below 768px) over .5s ease-in-out, so the letters sway gently. The halo type wraps the same bars in three layers (thick outline, mid outline, inner fill) to make sign lettering, and with amp: 0 it is used as a still logo.

options.text: Text to draw, defaults to the element’s aria-label or its text
options.gap: Gap ratio between bars within band height, default .22
options.stretch: Horizontal stretch (bar height stays the same), default 1 — use something like .7 when fitting a wide font to the wordmark proportions
options.amp: Wobble amount (rem — based on SVG coordinate height 160, same ratio as the original wordmark SVG), default .4 — 0 means no wobble
options.every: Tempo (ms) at which the bar picks a new position, default 1000
options.look: Sign lettering with a double outline around the halo face
options.--fx-bar: Bar fill (css), default text color (halo uses --kf-accent)
options.--fx-halo-out / --fx-halo-in: Outer·center border colors of halo (css), default --kf-ink · --kf-accent-soft
options.--fx-dur / --fx-ease: Slide duration and curve (css), default .5s · ease-in-out

note: Because the bars are made by slicing text, the bar ends may differ from the hand-finished typeface of the original — bold, wide sans-serifs (Rubik Mono One, Dela Gothic One) fit well. It is drawn once after all fonts have loaded, and the SVG stretches to the element width. The text stays hidden on screen so screen readers can read it
